summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console request-forensics, trace stitching, and error analysis for SolaceBI. Demonstrated request playback, KV cache fallback patterns, and how to map traces to customer logs. Discussed security (SOC2, SSO/SAML), VPC options and next steps for a short pilot.
topics: KV cache fallbacks and quantization impact
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-09
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Head of Platform, SolaceBI), Rina Patel (SRE Lead), Arun Mehta (CTO)

Auto Summary (generated): Quick console demo showing how to find a noisy endpoint, replay the failing request, and escalate with trace-to-log stitching. Security questions around data residency and SSO. Agreed to share security pack and run a two-week pilot on a seeded workload.

00:00 - Maya Chen: "Hey everyone, uh, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya — I'm the account lead. Luis is our systems engineer, he's gonna run through the console and the playback stuff. Um, do you want to do quick intros?"
00:14 - Daniel Park: "Sure — Daniel here, I run platform at SolaceBI. Rina's our SRE lead and Arun's our CTO. We're exploring solutions to reduce MTTR on model inference errors and get better request level visibility."
00:28 - Rina Patel: "Yep, hi all. We have high variance in latency and sometimes token-level hallucinations that are tricky to reproduce."
00:36 - Luis Ortega: "Cool. Today I'll show request mapping, trace stitching across microservices, and the KV cache fallback detective flow. There's a few gotchas I'll point out where transcriptions sometimes read K-V cache or key v cache in older exports — dont be surprised if you see that."
01:05 - Arun Mehta: "Two quick constraints up front — we need all logs to remain in our VPC for at-rest requirements and we follow a strict retention policy. Also SSO is required via SAML."
01:20 - Maya Chen: "Totally understood. We have Redwood Private and Dedicated options for that — we'll attach the SOC2 pack and the SAML setup guide. Luis, you want to kick the demo?"

05:02 - Luis Ortega: "Alright, here's the Console. I'm searching for a recent failing request ID that Daniel pasted earlier. You can see the request timeline: token generation, model variant used, and downstream calls to sentiment-service. Over on the right is a request-level cost and latency breakdown."
05:25 - Rina Patel: "Looks good — is that per-token trace for the model? We're used to seeing only coarse metrics."
05:31 - Luis Ortega: "It's a stitched view — the runtime emits a token-level trace that gets correlated with our sidecar traces. Sometimes the transcription layer mislabels numerical values; we see 'three two seven' instead of 327 — you'll see that in older exports."
06:10 - Daniel Park: "When you say stitch, how do you map to our existing OpenTelemetry traces?"
06:18 - Luis Ortega: "We propagate the same request id and you can drop in your OTEL collector. We also auto-link logs if they include the transaction id. There's a mapping UI where you can say this span equals this service. It is semi-automatic — it learns from your patterns."

12:40 - Luis Ortega: "Now I'm doing a request replay — console playback. It replays the exact prompt, headers, and model config. Important: playback can be run in dry-run mode or in isolated sandbox so it won't hit production downstream unless you toggle it."
12:58 - Rina Patel: "If we replay in sandbox, can it simulate the KV cache miss path? We see a lot of transient fallbacks when cache is cold and then latency spikes."
13:10 - Luis Ortega: "Yes — you can enable 'cache conditioning' in the playback config. We can either emulate a cold cache or force a miss to reproduce fallback behavior. For some models, quantization also changes the latency pattern and occasionally the token distribution, so we include model variant toggles."

18:45 - Arun Mehta: "Security: Where are these playback recordings stored? Does Redwood keep full PII?"
18:52 - Maya Chen: "Good question. By default hosted recordings live in our encrypted store, but for Private customers we can keep recordings inside your VPC. We have configurable redaction rules — you can scrub fields before storage. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration docs."
19:20 - Daniel Park: "And SSO? We use Okta."
19:24 - Maya Chen: "We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. We'll share the SAML metadata and a sample assertion mapping for Okta."

25:05 - Luis Ortega: "Back to tracing — here's an example where a long tail latency came from a fallback to a lower-tier model. In the timeline you can see at T+1.3s the runtime routed to a cheaper variant because primary pool was saturated, then at T+1.9s the KV cache returned and latency dropped. You can filter by routing policy and view rollout rules that triggered the fallback."
25:40 - Rina Patel: "How customizable are those routing policies? We sometimes split traffic based on org, endpoint, and latency buckets."
25:48 - Luis Ortega: "You can create policies by model, route, or tag. For Dedicated customers you get more granular control including capacity thresholds and region pinning."

32:15 - Daniel Park: "We'd want to attach our own logs — can we bring in our ELK or Datadog logs and correlate?"
32:24 - Luis Ortega: "Yes your existing logs can be ingested via the agent or by forwarding with our OTEL adapter. Once ingested we show a 'related logs' strip that links to the exact span that created the log. Occasionally the transcription engine mis-attributes speaker labels; you'll see 'Speaker 1' in some old exports, that's just the ASR."

38:01 - Luis Ortega: "Now I'll simulate an error path — payload exceeded token limit and we got a 413-like error. Console highlights the error, suggests probable root causes: tokenization issues, prompt concatenation bugs, or downstream truncation. It then shows a diff view of the last successful and first failing request to help diagnose."
38:30 - Rina Patel: "That's helpful. Does console automatically create an incident ticket?"
38:35 - Luis Ortega: "We can push incidents to your Jira with a payload that includes the request snapshot, relevant spans, and a link to the playback. Many customers wire that into their oncall workflow."

44:20 - Arun Mehta: "About pilot — we want to run a two-week pilot against a staging snapshot with seeded edge cases. Can Redwood run it inside our VPC?"
44:29 - Maya Chen: "Yes, Private mode can be deployed in your VPC. For a pilot we usually run Dedicated capacity but inside the customer's network boundary — we'll outline the infra checklist. It'll require a small infra change to open the collector and we'll share an ops-runbook."
44:55 - Daniel Park: "What sort of telemetry overhead should we expect?"
45:00 - Luis Ortega: "Trace baggage is minimal — token-level traces add an overhead but we do adaptive sampling for production and full capture for pilot. For the pilot you'll see slightly higher network egress for traces but it's controllable via sampling and retention windows."

51:02 - Rina Patel: "One more question on compliance — are audit logs immutable? We need an append-only ledger for a subset of events."
51:10 - Maya Chen: "We support write-once object storage configurations and can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Our audit export can be routed to your GCS/S3 bucket inside the VPC. We'll include a note in the security docs."

58:12 - Luis Ortega: "Recap — we demonstrated request-level playback with cache miss simulation, trace-to-log stitching for OTEL, routing policy visualization, and incident export. For the pilot we'll seed a staging workload and enable full capture for two weeks. I'll attach KV cache perf numbers and a sample playback config."
58:40 - Daniel Park: "Sounds good. Next steps are security docs, perf numbers, and a pilot proposal. I'll coordinate with our infra team on schedule."
58:55 - Maya Chen: "Great — I'll send over the SOC2 bundle and SAML guide by Monday. Luis will share perf spreadsheet midweek. We'll aim to kick off pilot week of 9/27 pending your infra go-ahead."
59:10 - Arun Mehta: "Perfect, thanks everyone."
59:15 - Meeting end

Notes on transcription quality: Several technical terms were sometimes transcribed oddly — e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'key V cache', numeric sequences sometimes expanded into words. Speaker labels are mostly correct but occasional 'Speaker 1' placeholders appeared in the raw export.

References shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (SOC2), https://redwood.ai/saml-quickstart, KV-cache-benchmarks.xlsx (shared by Luis), pilot-proposal-template.docx
